blocks.text: Hypothesis
A hypothesis is a testable statement or assumption about a population, situation, or relationship between variables.
Hypothesis Testing
Hypothesis testing is a statistical method used to decide whether there is enough evidence in sample data to support or reject a claim.
Null Hypothesis
The null hypothesis, written as (H_0), states that there is no significant difference, effect, or relationship between variables.
Alternative Hypothesis
The alternative hypothesis, written as (H_1) or (H_a), states that there is a significant difference, effect, or relationship between variables.
Test Statistic
A test statistic is a numerical value calculated from sample data and used to make a decision in hypothesis testing. Examples include (z), (t), and (F) values.
Critical Region
The critical region is the area in a statistical distribution where the null hypothesis is rejected.
Significance Level
The significance level, denoted by (\alpha), is the maximum probability of rejecting the null hypothesis when it is actually true. A common value is (0.05).

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: The symbol is printed as typesetting code, "(\alpha)"; it is the Greek letter α. In the same way (H_0), (H_1) and (H_a) above are printed code for H₀, H₁ and Hₐ.
p-value
The p-value shows the probability of obtaining the observed result, or a more extreme result, if the null hypothesis is true. A small p-value provides evidence against the null hypothesis.
Decision Rule
A decision rule is used to decide whether to reject or fail to reject the null hypothesis. For example, if (p-value < α), the null hypothesis is rejected.
Data Visualisation
Data visualization is the use of graphs, charts, and diagrams to present data clearly and support the interpretation of hypothesis testing results.
Bias
Bias is an unfair influence in data collection, analysis, or interpretation that may lead to incorrect or misleading conclusions.
Ethical Use of Data
Ethical use of data means collecting, analysing, and reporting data honestly, fairly, and responsibly while protecting privacy and avoiding misuse.
Communicating Results
Communicating results means presenting findings clearly, accurately, and in relation to the original hypothesis so that readers can understand the conclusion.
